subject.title: fix(agents): preserve target agent tool allowlist for subagents

question: May an explicitly configured target agent receive tools that are absent from the spawning parent’s effective tool set, or must the parent tool surface remain a hard delegation ceiling?
rationale: The current merged contract deliberately prevents delegated sessions from gaining a broader tool surface, while this PR changes that trust boundary to support specialized target agents; only maintainers can choose the intended authorization model.

options.title: Preserve parent ceiling
options.body: Keep inherited allow as a hard cap and solve privileged worker access through an explicitly authorized broker or future delegation capability.

options.title: Authorize target specialization
options.body: Define and approve a new explicit delegation contract that allows selected target agents to exceed the parent cap with security tests and upgrade documentation.

recommendation.title: Preserve parent ceiling
recommendation.body: Keep inherited allow as a hard cap and solve privileged worker access through an explicitly authorized broker or future delegation capability.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current delegated-session authorization contract and are the strongest history-backed owner for interpreting its security boundary.
